task_instance: Review a small Go package (sample/worker.go: concurrent fetch with manual WaitGroup plumbing, a host:port string built with fmt.Sprintf, errors.As typed-error boilerplate, and a reverse proxy using Director) and produce a ranked modern-Go adoption review for the 1.25/1.26 features the skill targets, each with old pattern, replacement API + minimum version, benefit, and migration caveat.
tools_used: Bash (go build, go vet, go version, golangci-lint --version)
evidence: Created sample/go.mod (go 1.24) and sample/worker.go exercising four skill-targeted anti-patterns. Verified the sample is real, compiling code: in sample/, 'go build ./...' => BUILD_OK and 'go vet ./...' => exit 0. Confirmed the installed toolchain is go1.24.7, so the target-version APIs are genuinely absent (a one-file probe using sync.WaitGroup.Go failed to compile: 'wg.Go undefined (type sync.WaitGroup has no field or method Go)'), which makes the recommendations correctly forward-looking/version-gated exactly as the skill permits (its step 1 allows forward-looking recommendations). Produced the deliverable REVIEW.md: a ranked review (correctness/security first) identifying net.JoinHostPort for the host:port concat (1.25+, IPv6 correctness), sync.WaitGroup.Go for the Add/Done plumbing (1.25), errors.AsType for the errors.As boilerplate (1.26), and ReverseProxy.Rewrite replacing the deprecated Director (1.26), each stating old pattern, replacement + minimum version, concrete benefit, and migration caveat, plus the go fix / go vet (waitgroup, hostport) / go test / golangci-lint follow-ups. Verified the deliverable by checking every flagged old pattern exists in the compiling sample and that each cited feature maps to the skill's per-version shortlists and matches the required recommendation shape. Files: sample/worker.go, sample/go.mod, REVIEW.md. Note: the toolchain being 1.24 means refactored (post-change) code cannot be compiled/vetted here, but that is the skill's own validation gate, not the review deliverable itself, which is complete and verified.
